summary:
Your volume is locked in at a plateau right now — 127 km over the last four weeks versus 125 km the prior block, essentially flat — but the distribution within that tells a more interesting story. Today's 13.77 km at 5:48/km with HR 137 sits comfortably aerobic, and paired with Monday's 11.73 km at 5:59/km, you've run back-to-back days at controlled effort, which is exactly the durability stimulus that compounds quietly over weeks.

The standout anchor from recent data is June 27th: 15.73 km at 4:49/km with HR 161, a load score nearly three times your typical easy run. That's threshold-adjacent work at a pace meaningfully faster than your 10K PB pace would suggest you'd sustain for 15+ km without racing — worth noting as a signal that your speed-end capacity is in good shape, not just your base. Your lactate threshold is now formally logged at 4:24/km @ 178 bpm, and with only today's value in the 30-day baseline, it'll take a few more comparable efforts before trend analysis is meaningful there.

Strength frequency remains the variable to watch — 4 sessions across the last four weeks is functional but on the lower end of what you've been targeting, and a 3-week streak suggests you're rebuilding consistency rather than in full rhythm. Steps average of 14,120/day including 11,641 on rest days indicates your background load is genuinely non-trivial, which partly offsets any session-count shortfall.
